subject: Execution footprint attestation & erase-proof request: regions, subprocessors, and deletion evidence
messages:
From: Alison Park <alison.park@ledgerflow.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:13:00-05:00
Subject: Evidence request: execution footprint and deletion proofs

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — LedgerFlow's Security & Legal teams are moving quickly and have a compact evidence checklist for the next phase of evaluation. Can you help with the following items so we can close the compliance review?

- A current breakdown of where inference requests are executed (region-level) for our production tenant and any transient hops to subprocessors.
- A list of subprocessors involved in request execution, indicating which ones may be outside the US.
- Proof that deletion requests issued via API/console remove transient caches and are not just logical markers (logs or audit entries are fine).
- Any signed attestation we can include in our vendor pack that confirms deletion behavior and KMS boundaries.

If you can send a short packet (docs + a couple of logs/attestation), our LegalOps team will review and confirm next steps. We need this by end-of-week if possible.

Appreciate it —
Alison
LedgerFlow, Security

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@ledgerflow.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: execution footprint and deletion proofs

Hi Alison —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a concise packet. For visibility: Jordan (Product) is looped in for the execution-region mapping.

Initial plan:
- Attach a current subprocessor snapshot (redwood_subproc_snapshot_v1.csv) showing active runtime partners, their processing regions, and contract classification.
- Provide a short write-up on transient KV/prefix caching and how our automated wipe works on delete requests.
- Include redacted deletion audit entries demonstrating end-to-end removal from cache + runtime logs.
- If Legal needs a signed attestation, we can produce a one-page attestation that includes KMS region boundaries and statement of delete behavior; that will require signature from our Head of Security.

Two quick clarifying questions so we match your expectations:
1) Do you need production-level logs (redacted) or is an example deletion trace sufficient for now?
2) Is LedgerFlow required to see the raw KMS key region IDs or is a region-level indication (US-East, US-West) enough?

I'll get the subprocessor snapshot attached now. Follow-up packet with logs and draft attestation by tomorrow.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subproc_snapshot_v1.csv (CSV)

From: LegalOps <legalops@ledgerflow.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Alison Park <alison.park@ledgerflow.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: execution footprint and deletion proofs

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- For now, an example deletion trace is acceptable, but if it moves toward procurement we'll ask for a production-redacted set.
- Region-level KMS info is fine; we do not need raw key IDs.
- Please include any contractual subprocessor classifications (subprocessor vs. managed partner) and whether subprocessors process plaintext inputs or only encrypted payloads.

I've attached our short evidence checklist to make sure we cover everything on our end. If possible, include a signed attestation PDF and any exportable audit logs showing the deletion operation and the TTL/eviction in the runtime.

Thanks —
LegalOps Team (LedgerFlow)

Attachment: ledgerflow_evidence_checklist.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: LegalOps <legalops@ledgerflow.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:12:00-05:00
Subject: RE: Evidence request: execution footprint and deletion proofs

Hi Alison / LegalOps team —

Appreciate the checklist. Per item:

1) Subprocessors & regions: attached is the exported subprocessor snapshot and a brief matrix (redwood_subproc_snapshot_v1.csv). Key points:
   - Core inference runtime: Redwood-managed, runs in customer-configured cloud regions (US-East, US-West).
   - Edge optimizer partner (EdgeScale): transiently touches request metadata for routing; processing region: US-West and EU-West (only for customers who enable multi-region).
   - Embedding store partner (VectorStoreCo): stores encrypted embeddings; processing region: US-East; note: embeddings are encrypted at rest using customer-bound KMS.

2) Deletion proof: we are attaching a signed attestation (attestation_signed_20261122.pdf) and a sample deletion trace which contains: a deletion API call, the runtime cache eviction entry, and an audit row showing the final tombstone + tombstone purge job run. We will not include raw PII.

3) KMS info: included kms_key_regions.csv which maps logical KMS regions (US-East, US-West) to our deployment zones. No raw key material is shared.

4) Attestation: the attached PDF is an internal-attestation template signed by our Security Director. It includes the statements you requested about deletion behavior and KMS boundaries. If LedgerFlow needs a different phrasing for procurement, tell us and we can produce a tailored attestation.

Quote from Alison's earlier request: "Proof that deletion requests issued via API/console remove transient caches and are not just logical markers (logs or audit entries are fine)." The sample trace shows exactly that flow.

Let us know if you need additional redactions or an expanded production export.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Product Security Liaison, Redwood Inference

Attachments: attestation_signed_20261122.pdf, kms_key_regions.csv

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: LegalOps <legalops@ledgerflow.com>, Alison Park <alison.park@ledgerflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T15:42:00-05:00
Subject: Final packet: attestation + sample deletion export and next steps

Hi Alison / LegalOps —

Following up with the consolidated packet attached. Summary of items included and next steps:

- Subprocessor matrix: redwood_subproc_snapshot_v1.csv (exported list with roles and regions).
- Signed attestation: attestation_signed_20261122.pdf (statement on deletion behavior + KMS region boundaries, signed by Security Director).
- KMS region map: kms_key_regions.csv (region-level mapping only).
- Sample deletion evidence: redwood_delete-proof-logs-20261123.zip (contains redacted runtime eviction trace, deletion API call record, and the purge job audit row).

Next steps proposed:
- LegalOps to confirm whether the attestation language is sufficient for procurement. If not, send edits and we will have Security sign the tailored version.
- If LedgerFlow needs a production-redacted log export, we can schedule a secure transfer; that will require a short SoW addendum and a date for the export window.

If everything looks good, we can mark this story closed and move toward final contract. Jordan will assist on any technical follow-ups.

Thanks for the collaboration — please acknowledge receipt and we will hand off to Security/Legal for signature validation if required.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_delete-proof-logs-20261123.zip
